analyst.summary: IndusInd Bank is recovering from a self-inflicted 2025 crisis — incorrect derivative accounting plus separate microfinance-book irregularities that forced a Rs 2,329 crore loss in one quarter and cost the CEO and deputy CEO their jobs. A year on, the numbers are healing: the bank returned to profit, capital is comfortable, a new CEO (ex-Axis Bank) has been in the seat for almost a year, and the microfinance stress that was the other big worry is visibly improving quarter on quarter. What is not yet closed is the regulator-ordered probe into who is individually accountable for the lapses, and profitability (return on equity) is still far below what this bank used to generate. The stock, at roughly book value, is already priced for a fairly complete recovery rather than for a discount — so we see it as a hold, not a name to exit, but also not one to add to without seeing the still-pending accountability outcome and the next quarter's numbers (due within days) confirm the recovery is durable.
